content.value_statement: Research work is hard to assess consistently across rigor, evidence, and presentation. This skill applies ScholarEval rubrics to produce structured scores, strengths, weaknesses, and revision priorities.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates research papers, proposals, literature reviews, theses, and conference abstracts.
Applies rubrics for research questions, literature, methods, data, analysis, writing, and citations.
Produces strengths, weaknesses, critical issues, and prioritized recommendations.
Supports optional 1 to 5 scoring for each evaluation dimension.
Uses a Python calculator to aggregate dimension scores with default or custom weights.
Assesses publication readiness for a target venue when context is provided.
limitations: It does not replace expert peer review or discipline-specific judgment.
Scores depend on the completeness and quality of the submitted work.
Some dimensions may not apply to theoretical or early-stage work.
The score calculator writes reports to the output path supplied by the user.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Journal Submission
use_cases.description: Assess a draft article against rigor, contribution, presentation, and readiness expectations before submission.

use_cases.title: Improve a Thesis Chapter
use_cases.description: Identify strengths, weak sections, and revision priorities for a thesis or dissertation chapter.

use_cases.title: Screen Research Quality
use_cases.description: Compare proposals or manuscripts using consistent evaluation dimensions and transparent scoring rationale.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Scholarly Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single paper.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this research paper with ScholarEval. Give an overall assessment, three strengths, three weaknesses, and the top revision priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Methodology Review
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess only the methodology, data collection, and analysis sections. Explain whether the design fits the research questions and where rigor is weak.

prompt_templates.title: Score a Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Score each applicable ScholarEval dimension from 1 to 5. Provide evidence for each score and calculate an overall recommendation.

prompt_templates.title: Publication Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this manuscript for the target venue. Compare its contribution, rigor, writing, and citations against publication expectations, then prioritize fixes.

output_examples.input: A draft empirical paper with methods, results, and discussion sections.
output: Overall quality is good, with strong research questions and clear results.
The main weakness is limited justification for sample size and missing robustness checks.
Priority revisions are methodology justification, clearer limitations, and stronger citation balance.

output_examples.input: A literature review chapter for a dissertation.
output: Coverage is broad, but synthesis is uneven across themes.
The review should state the research gap earlier and compare competing findings directly.
A revised structure should group sources by argument, not only by topic.

output_examples.input: A conference abstract for a new research idea.
output: The idea is promising, but the contribution is not yet distinct from recent work.
Clarify the baseline, expected evidence, and practical impact before submission.

best_practices: Provide the full work, target venue, discipline, and development stage before evaluation.
Ask for evidence tied to sections, pages, claims, or tables.
Use scores together with written rationale, not as standalone judgments.
anti_patterns: Asking for an acceptance decision from only an abstract.
Treating the rubric score as a replacement for expert review.
Ignoring the discipline, venue, and stage of the work.

faq.question: What types of scholarly work can it evaluate?
faq.answer: It can evaluate papers, proposals, literature reviews, thesis chapters, abstracts, and related scholarly drafts.

faq.question: Does it provide numeric scores?
faq.answer: Yes. It can score each applicable dimension from 1 to 5 and explain the rationale.

faq.question: Can it review only one section?
faq.answer: Yes. You can request a targeted review of methodology, writing, citations, or another dimension.

faq.question: Does it replace peer review?
faq.answer: No. It supports structured feedback, but expert review remains necessary for final scholarly judgment.

faq.question: Can it compare drafts over time?
faq.answer: Yes. Reuse the same dimensions and scoring scale to track revision progress.

faq.question: Does the score calculator need a specific input format?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects dimension names with scores from 1 to 5 in a JSON file.
